newsitem.title: FRANCE: French company withdraws meals in madcow scare. [CORRECTED 12:34 GMT]
newsitem.headline: French company withdraws meals in madcow scare. [CORRECTED 12:34 GMT]

text.p: A French food company on Monday withdrew a range of prepared meals which may contain British beef because they were made before British beef imports were banned to prevent the spread of mad cow disease.
A spokesman for Panzani-William, a subsidiary of food group Danone, said the meals had been sold under the brand name William Saurin, one of France's most popular brands of such dishes.
"There is no reason for panicking. These are harmless products," the spokesman told radio France-Info.
He said the meals already bought could be exchanged for new ones. They included beef meals as well as spaghettis in Bolognese beef sauce and canellonis.
The European Union banned British beef exports last March to protect public health and restore consumer confidence in beef.

The ban was imposed after London raised fears that humans who ate the meat of animals infected with the Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) might become ill with the brain-wasting Creuzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD).
Meanwhile, the French Agriculture Ministry said the country had registered its 25th (Corrects from 20th) case of mad cow disease in six years.
A spokeswoman said the case was registered in the north of Brittany, the western region most affected by the disease.
She said the whole 65-strong herd was slaughtered.
